quote: 245.5 ED visits per 10,000 for suicide ideation and self-harm
correct_fact: AHS measure is 245.5 per 10,000 ED VISITS (share of ED visits), not per 10,000 residents; AHS June 2026 report updates it to 230.9. Same phrase appears 4x in the book (Ch8 x3, plus one later chapter at docx offset ~619,000).
source_quote: ED Visits for Suicide Ideation or Self-Harm per 10,000 ED Visits 245.5 ... Two hundred forty-six of every 10,000 ED visits from January to mid-October 2025 were attributed to suicide ideation or self-harm.

quote: the most sophisticated all-payer primary care transformation program in the country
correct_fact: Superlative with no source; neutralize.

quote: All-Payer / Medicare + Medicaid + Commercial
correct_fact: Medicare stopped contributing to Blueprint payments when the All-Payer ACO Model agreement ended Dec 2025; the state backfilled for CY2026. Stat card contradicts the chapter's own text (line 3764).
source_quote: Once the agreement ends, Medicare will no longer be able to contribute payments to Blueprint programs until another agreement with CMS is signed.

correct_fact: 5.8 = Jones et al., Popul Health Manag 2016;19(3):196-205 ('$5.8 million for every $1 million', annualized cost-gain ratio, 2008-2013 data) and DVHA 2016 all-payer CY2014 estimate 5.8; 91% personal health care provider (2023 BRFSS, AHS Nov 2025). Blueprint statute 2006. Note later estimates are lower (see 8.9 finding).
source_quote: medical expenditures decreased by approximately $5.8 million for every $1 million spent on the Blueprint initiative

quote: It is, in the view of most independent analysts, the most successful sustained primary care transformation initiative in American health policy.
correct_fact: No source for an analyst consensus or the superlative; delete.

quote: Blueprint program funding through DVHA; supplemented by OneCare (now transitioning), Medicaid, and grant funding
correct_fact: CHT payments come from Medicaid and commercial insurers (Medicare until Dec 2025, state-backfilled for 2026) plus Blueprint program funding; OneCare has wound down.
source_quote: This agreement has allowed Medicare to participate in the Blueprint by contributing practice payments and CHT payments.

quote: six-year longitudinal study using VHCURES all-payer claims data published in Population Health Management ... $5.8 million for every $1 million
correct_fact: Jones C, Finison K, McGraves-Lloyd K, et al. Popul Health Manag 2016;19(3):196-205: 6-year sequential cross-sectional, 2008-2013; -$482 per person DiD; driven by inpatient (-$218) and outpatient hospital expenditures; inpatient discharges -8.8/1000; 9 of 11 quality measures higher. The 'most rigorous' superlative is unsupported.
source_quote: Using a 6-year, sequential, cross-sectional methodology ... medical expenditures decreased by approximately $5.8 million for every $1 million spent on the Blueprint initiative

quote: The most rigorous evaluation
correct_fact: Superlative unsourced; call it 'A peer-reviewed evaluation'.

quote: that Oliver Wyman identified as the largest source of indirect savings
correct_fact: Oliver Wyman lists primary-care access and SDOH among 'Sources of Indirect Savings' without ranking them.
source_quote: Sources of Indirect Savings (to system) ... Expand access to primary care settings to manage patient needs ... Some emergency visits are preventable

quote: Medicare specifically found statistically significant healthcare savings
correct_fact: CMS MAPCP final evaluation (RTI 2017) as summarized by Blueprint: $64M Medicare net savings over 14 quarters in Vermont, return on fees 4.49.
source_quote: the MAPCP Demonstration resulted in $64 million in Medicare savings relative to PCMH comparison practices

quote: Blueprint quality data 2023 --- maintained above national average

quote: has operated since 2010 under a CMS Multi-Payer Advanced Primary Care Practice Demonstration that allowed Medicare to participate in PCMH and CHT payments. That Medicare participation ended in December 2025 with the All-Payer ACO Model agreement
correct_fact: Vermont entered MAPCP in 2010 (per AHS AHEAD application), but MAPCP ended in 2016; from 2017 Medicare's Blueprint payments continued under the All-Payer ACO Model agreement, which ended Dec 2025. $10.8M CY2026 bridge confirmed (VMS: secured; $4.45M GF).
source_quote: In December of 2025, the current all-payer model agreement ... will end. This agreement has allowed Medicare to participate in the Blueprint (Blueprint 2025 Annual Report)

quote: 68% after SUD ED visits
correct_fact: AHS measure is 30-day follow-up after ED visit for ALCOHOL USE (68% summary table; 67% in appendix), PCMH-attributed patients, 2023 Blueprint via VHCURES — not all SUD. Appendix E already says '68% (alcohol use) (2023)'. 76% MI figure matches AHS summary table (Appendix D of same report shows 81%).
source_quote: 30-Day Follow-Up After ED Visit for Mental Illness 76% ... 30-Day Follow-Up After ED Visit for Alcohol Use 68%

correct_fact: DMH pages give 6 or 7 designated hospitals; the state-run psychiatric hospital is Vermont Psychiatric Care Hospital (Berlin), not the Retreat. correct_fact: No source found for 80%. Blueprint 2025 Annual Report: as of Nov 15, 2025, 119 practices (93% of PCMHs) in Year 2; 62.2 FTE funded by MHI; 'All HSAs have hired staff'. Same 80% claim in Fig 8.3 (count 2: Ch8 table + a repeat).
source_quote: a total of 62.2 FTE staff positions are currently providing care thanks to the MHI funding ... All HSAs have hired staff, giving the Pilot statewide reach.

quote: "The MHI initiative allowed primary care teams to serve more patients and provide more consistent follow-up. Flexible and team-based care models helped patients engage in services, particularly those facing complex medical and social challenges."
correct_fact: The qualitative evaluation exists (Market Decisions Research; final report on Blueprint MHI webpage per 2025 Annual Report) but the quoted wording could not be located online. Verify against the report or delete the pull quote; no replacement text proposed.
